title: Key points - Protection of creative works and sports content : intensification and expansion to new stakeholders
text:
## Key points

March 2026 
No. 28 

### Protection of creative works and sports content: intensification and expansion to new stakeholders

Since 2022, Arcom’s efforts to combat the dissemination of illegal cultural and sports content have continued to intensify. The joint action of rights holders, judicial authorities and Arcom has proven effective, resulting in a 34% decrease in overall illegal consumption between 2021 and 2025. Legal proceedings brought by rights holders against new categories of technical intermediaries have broadened anti-piracy efforts by targeting services such as alternative DNS resolvers and VPN providers, which may be used by internet users to circumvent blocking measures.

Arcom’s blocking requests now also extend to these new actors. At the same time, Arcom has continued its efforts to improve the visibility of legal content, in order to promote copyright-compliant consumption practices. Nevertheless, the persistence of illegal prac tices and their rapid adaptation to enforcement measures require the ongoing development of antipiracy tools. Accordingly, combating piracy now requires strengthening technical, legal and cooperative mechanisms among the various stakeholders involved.

#### / Intensified action against unlawful cultural services

In 2025, the number of requests to block domain names associated with initially blocked sites (or “mirror sites”) increased by 37%, reaching 1,154 blocked domain names, representing nearly half of all blockings since 2022. An increasing share of measures targets IPTV services (391 domain names blocked).

Focus on actions by rights holders Arcom’s activities form part of a broader framework in which rights holders play a full role – particularly in the audiovisual sector, such as the Association de lutte contre la piraterie audiovisuelle (ALPA) and members of the Association pour la protection des programmes sportifs (APPS). Beyond the initial actions enabling the blocking of unlawful sites, which are then updated on an ongoing basis by Arcom, rights holders may also undertake legal action directly targeting unlawful hosting services (or cyberlockers), as was the case in 2023, when action initiated through the ACE coalition (Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment) resulted in the closure of Uptobox.

##### 2,583 mirror sites blocked at Arcom’s request since 2022

Arcom has also undertaken coordinated actions with certain rights holders targeting “galaxies” of services (a galaxy being defined by the initial domain name and its mirror sites, i.e. all domain names associated with a single brand or name), which are particularly popular among internet users and have led to a significant decrease in the audience of these services (notably Wawacity and Zone-Téléchargement). Since 2024, these actions have concerned exclusively the audiovisual sector.

#### / Increased involvement of all intermediaries in tackling illegal sports streaming

Since 1 October 2022, referrals received by Arcom have resulted in the blocking of 12,606 domain names (in addition to the 1,657 domain names blocked pursuant to initial court decisions). The year 2025 alone accounts for more than half of all blockings, with 6,496 domain names blocked, an increase of 71% compared with the previous year.

##### 6,496 sites blocked at Arcom’s request in 2025

##### Involvement of new intermediaries

In response to the misuse of tools such as domain name resolution services (alternative DNS) and virtual private network (VPN) providers by internet users, sports rights holders have expanded the list of technical intermediaries targeted in legal proceedings beyond internet service providers (ISPs), focusing on the largest of these actors.

The implementation of measures ordered by Arcom varies significantly depending on the intermediaries concerned. Constructive discussions between Arcom and Google are to be welcomed, with Google imple menting blocking measures diligently at the level of its DNS service. Similarly, discussions are ongoing with other stakeholders in order to improve the han dling of notifications issued by Arcom. Conversely, certain intermediaries, notably Cloudflare, only partially implement Arcom’s blocking requests: only 8% of the requests notified to Cloudflare are effectively implemented.

As part of efforts to combat mirror sites, a provision in the draft law aimed at strengthening the film sector provides for expanding the list of persons authorised to refer matters to Arcom, as well as simplifying its internal procedures by allowing decisions to be taken by its Chair or a designated member of the Board. Having been adopted by the Senate, this provision is supported by Arcom for adoption by the National Assembly. Similarly, Arcom supports the provisions set out in the draft law on the organisation, management and financing of professional sport, adopted at first reading by the Senate on 10 June 2025, aimed at strengthening efforts to combat sports content piracy. These measures notably introduce a real-time dynamic blocking mechanism targeting unlawful services broadcasting sports content, designed to facilitate IP address blocking in addition to the DNS blocking measures under the current framework.

Arcom continues to encourage rights holders and technical intermediaries to conclude agreements to enhance cooperation and streamline and expedite the implementation of measures ordered by the courts and Arcom. The involvement of responsible stakeholders could also be strengthened by enabling Arcom to share the list of blocked domain names with voluntary participants, which is currently not possible under existing legislation. The Digital Services Act (DSA) also provides fur ther opportunities that should be fully leveraged, including trusted flagger status, the provisions of Article 9 relating to orders addressed to digital intermediaries and mechanisms for cooperation between authorities.

Continuation of work on IP blocking

Française des Télécoms (FFTélécoms – namely Orange, Bouygues Telecom and SFR), joined by the Iliad group, with a view to implementing an automated “IP blocking” solution, constituted a significant step forward in this process.

#### / A regulatory model that needs to adapt to emerging developments to enhance its effectiveness and agility

While Arcom’s action has demonstrated its effectiveness, the fight against piracy now calls for continued adaptation to evolving consumption patterns. The publication, in December 2025, of a report on anti-piracy instruments 1, prepared at the request of the Chair of the National Assembly’s Committee on Cultural Affairs and Education, has helped to set out the key challenges ahead.
